architectural_implications.after: Agent issues one task-scoped context request; the engine merges sources, ranks by relevance, resolves conflicts and filters by permission before anything reaches the model.
architectural_implications.before: Agent is wired directly to Slack MCP, Linear MCP and GitHub MCP servers and must reconcile conflicting matches inside its own context window.
architectural_implications.consequence: Smaller, cleaner prompts and lower token cost, but a new component whose latency, freshness and failure modes now sit on the critical path of every agent action.
architectural_implications.observation: Where context synthesis lives determines how much reasoning the model does about sources rather than about the task.

architectural_implications.after: The context engine enforces permissions as a first-class stage of context delivery.
architectural_implications.before: Each tool/data connection enforces its own ACLs, and the agent is trusted to not over-share what it retrieves.
architectural_implications.consequence: Security becomes centrally auditable and consistent across agents, but the engine must model every source's authorization semantics — making it a high-value and high-blast-radius dependency.
architectural_implications.observation: Permission enforcement moves from prompt-level trust to a centralized delivery-path gate.

architectural_implications.after: Rationale, decisions and post-mortems are captured and delivered as structured context at agent runtime.
architectural_implications.before: A human reviews background agent output to supply the missing 'why', acting as the context layer.
architectural_implications.consequence: Unattended background agents become viable, but only if institutional decision history is actually written down and kept current — otherwise the silent-failure risk simply becomes invisible.
architectural_implications.observation: Human babysitting is an implicit context layer that can be removed only when curation is explicit.

architectural_implications.after: Context assembly is a distinct layer with its own inputs (sources, conflicts, permissions) and outputs (synthesized, ranked snippets) that can be evaluated in isolation.
architectural_implications.before: Agent quality is evaluated holistically as a single end-to-end outcome.
architectural_implications.consequence: Enables context-specific evals — coverage, contradiction handling, staleness — and lets teams swap models or frameworks without re-validating their entire knowledge pipeline.
architectural_implications.observation: Context quality becomes a separable, benchmarkable concern from model and runtime choice.

article_ideas.angle: Start from the async-dispatch ticket example, then generalize: what retrieval systems index versus what decisions they must index, and what a decision record needs to contain to suppress a bad recommendation.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and platform/DevOps leads deploying background agents into existing codebases
article_ideas.based_on: The highest-cost context gap is negative knowledge
article_ideas.thesis: The dominant agent failure is not reasoning quality but the absence of negative knowledge: agents confidently revert deliberate decisions because no system stores prohibitions and their rationale, and fixing this requires a new data class, not a better prompt.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Doesn't Need a Bigger Model, It Needs a Record of What You Turned Off

article_ideas.angle: Argue against the integration-count scoreboard; show the mechanism (raw matches, conflicting sources, agent-side arbitration) and where a synthesis stage belongs architecturally.
article_ideas.audience: Engineering managers and agent platform teams evaluating MCP rollouts
article_ideas.thesis: MCP is necessary but insufficient: each additional connected source raises recall and lowers signal-to-noise, pushing source adjudication and token cost onto the model — so connectivity without a ranking-and-reconciliation layer is a quality regression disguised as progress.
article_ideas.title: Adding Integrations Made My Agent Worse

article_ideas.angle: Reframe human-in-the-loop from a safety practice into an accounting entry, and propose instrumenting review time to attribute it to missing context rather than to model weakness.
article_ideas.audience: Teams running background agents and deciding whether to remove human review
article_ideas.based_on: Humans currently act as the context layer by babysitting agents
article_ideas.thesis: Human review of agent output is an implicit, unscalable context layer; the hours spent supplying missing rationale are a measurable proxy for context defects, and treating review time as a KPI converts an invisible cost into an engineering backlog.
article_ideas.title: Babysitting Is Your Context Debt Metric

article_ideas.angle: Map the nine runtime requirements to what frameworks now cover, then show what is left over: per-task ranking, permission filtering and context freshness, which have far less tooling.
article_ideas.audience: Staff engineers and technical leads planning agent roadmaps and headcount
article_ideas.thesis: As frameworks absorb session management, sandboxing, observability and replay, engineering differentiation migrates to data relevance and workflow design — teams still building bespoke runtime plumbing are paying for solved problems while leaving context unowned.
article_ideas.title: The Runtime Is Solved; Your Relevance Problem Is Not

connections.relationship: Layered rather than competing: MCP supplies access/transport, the context engine supplies synthesis, ranking, reconciliation and permission enforcement on top of it.
Reveals a class of memory most systems omit — records of deliberate non-actions — whose absence causes agents to confidently revert prior fixes.
Permission filtering must happen in the retrieval-and-delivery path, not in prompt instructions, because context is assembled per user and per task.
Background agent errors produce no exception, so observability must measure artifact plausibility and context coverage rather than tool-call success.
If agent definition reduces to model + instructions + tools + sandbox, investment shifts from runtime plumbing to context curation and workflow design.

evidence_quotes.text: a Context Engine synthesizes sources, ranks by task relevance, resolves contradictions, and enforces permissions
A Context Engine delivers a synthesized understanding that an agent can act on directly.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent operating over multiple heterogeneous organizational systems will eventually need a synthesis layer; relying on the model to adjudicate raw multi-source retrieval pushes an unbounded reasoning and token cost into every call.
core_insights.insight: Context assembly should be a distinct architectural layer (a "Context Engine") sitting between the agent and data sources, responsible for merging signals across code, docs, tickets and conversations, ranking by task relevance, resolving contradictions, enforcing permissions, and delivering a synthesized result rather than raw matches.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It relocates responsibility for relevance, conflict resolution and ACL enforcement out of the agent's prompt and into a dedicated, testable service — changing where the hard engineering lives and making context quality independently measurable from model quality.

evidence_quotes.text: MCP is great at access, but access isn't understanding.
MCP floods the agent with raw matches, increasing context window costs and forcing the agent to decide what to believe.
Connecting multiple MCP servers without a context layer floods agents with irrelevant raw data.

core_insights.generalization: Adding integrations increases recall but decreases signal-to-noise; without a ranking/reconciliation step, more connected sources can make agent output worse and more expensive, not better.
core_insights.insight: MCP provides reach without understanding: connecting multiple MCP servers returns raw matches that inflate the context window and force the agent itself to decide which sources to believe, which is a distinct failure mode from missing access.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes tool-connectivity work as necessary-but-insufficient, and predicts a specific degradation pattern (token bloat plus agent-side arbitration between conflicting sources) that appears precisely when teams scale from one MCP server to several.

evidence_quotes.text: An AI agent fixing a linear ticket recommended reenabling async dispatch because it lacked context that a support engineer had explicitly disabled it due to a past outage.
Agents operating without organizational context will repeat past mistakes and cause outages.

core_insights.generalization: Context systems optimized for retrieval of what exists systematically under-index what was intentionally removed or forbidden; agents then treat absence of evidence as permission.
core_insights.insight: The highest-cost context gap is negative knowledge — the record that something was deliberately disabled or rejected and why (post-mortems, prior decisions, tribal knowledge). An agent without it doesn't abstain; it confidently proposes reverting the fix.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It implies context stores must capture decision rationale and prohibitions, not just documents and code, and that 'no relevant results' is a dangerous state rather than a neutral one for autonomous agents.

evidence_quotes.text: Without proper context, background agents make silent mistakes that misinform teams.
Humans currently act as the context layer by babysitting agents.
The gap is not intelligence. It's context.

core_insights.generalization: As agents move from synchronous chat to asynchronous background execution, the dominant risk shifts from visible wrong answers to plausible-but-unfounded artifacts propagating through team workflows; the fix is upstream context quality, not better prompting.
core_insights.insight: Background agents fail silently: without context they produce confident, wrong artifacts that misinform teams, and the current industry mitigation is a human acting as a manual context layer by babysitting the agent.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It identifies the human-in-the-loop as an unscalable workaround masking a context defect, and points to a specific observability gap — errors that never surface as exceptions because the agent never knew it was wrong.

evidence_quotes.text: Building agents is trivial now. Context is the next frontier.
defining an agent requires only selecting a model, setting instructions, defining tools and skills, and choosing sandbox locations
Building agent infrastructure is no longer a major engineering hurdle thanks to modern frameworks.

core_insights.generalization: When a layer commoditizes, competitive effort migrates one level up the stack; teams still investing in bespoke runtime plumbing are paying for solved problems.
core_insights.insight: Agent runtime infrastructure (session management, checkpointing, orchestration, retries, sandbox isolation, observability, multi-channel adapters, replay) has been absorbed by frameworks, collapsing an agent definition to model selection, instructions, tools/skills, and sandbox choice.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If the definition of an agent is now a few declarative parameters, engineering differentiation cannot come from the runtime; it must come from workflow design and data relevance, which reorders what teams should staff and measure.

evidence_quotes.text: Ensures agents receive precise, permissioned, and timely information without polluting context windows.
Targeted retrieval
Personalized relevance
Permission enforcement

core_insights.generalization: Retrieval quality is a function of the request, not of the corpus; any context system with a single global index will over- or under-serve most tasks and will leak data across permission boundaries.
core_insights.insight: Context delivery is per-task and per-user, not a static index: the same source corpus must be re-ranked for relevance to the specific task, personalized to the requesting user, and filtered to that user's permissions at query time.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It means context engineering is a runtime ranking-and-authorization problem with its own latency budget and per-call cost, not a one-off ingestion/indexing job — and that permission enforcement must live in the delivery path, not in the agent's prompt.

evidence_quotes.text: An AI agent fixing a linear ticket recommended reenabling async dispatch because it lacked context that a support engineer had explicitly disabled it due to a past outage.
Agents operating without organizational context will repeat past mistakes and cause outages.

deep_dives.research_question: What record structure makes prohibitions and prior decisions machine-actionable enough that an agent actively suppresses a plausible but previously-rejected change?
deep_dives.topic: Negative knowledge as a first-class context class
deep_dives.why: Retrieval indexes what exists and systematically under-indexes what was deliberately removed, so agents treat absence of evidence as permission and re-propose changes that previously caused outages.

evidence_quotes.text: MCP provides access, but access is not understanding.

deep_dives.research_question: How do task accuracy and token cost change as connected MCP server count rises from 1 to 3 to 5, with and without a ranking/reconciliation stage?
deep_dives.topic: Scaling behavior of raw MCP access versus a synthesis layer
deep_dives.why: It tests the falsifiable core claim that more connectivity can make agents worse and more expensive, and locates the crossover point where a context layer becomes mandatory rather than optional.

evidence_quotes.text: Without proper context, background agents make silent mistakes that misinform teams.
Agents lack a full picture because they miss tribal knowledge and post-mortem discussions.

deep_dives.research_question: Can an eval suite detect a missing-context defect before deployment when the agent produces a confident, non-exceptional, wrong artifact?
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How do you evaluate context coverage and detect a missing-context failure before deployment?
deep_dives.why: Silent failures never surface as tool-call errors, so standard end-to-end correctness evals are blind to them; context coverage must become a separately measured property of the pipeline.

evidence_quotes.text: Ensures agents receive precise, permissioned, and timely information without polluting context windows.
Permission enforcement

deep_dives.research_question: What does it cost to enforce per-user permissions as a retrieval-stage gate rather than as prompt-level trust, and how does that gate behave when sources disagree about authorization semantics?
deep_dives.topic: Permission enforcement in the context delivery path
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Permission enforcement moves from prompt-level trust to a centralized delivery-path gate
deep_dives.why: Centralizing ACL filtering makes security auditable across all agents, but it places a high-blast-radius component on the critical path of every agent action and requires modeling each source's authorization model.

evidence_quotes.text: a Context Engine synthesizes sources, ranks by task relevance, resolves contradictions, and enforces permissions
Agents lack a full picture because they miss tribal knowledge and post-mortem discussions.

deep_dives.research_question: Which event signals (commits, ticket closures, incident post-mortems) should invalidate a stored decision record, and how much staleness-induced error does invalidation actually remove?
deep_dives.topic: Freshness and invalidation of decision rationale
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How does a context engine keep tribal knowledge current as decisions change in real time?
deep_dives.why: A context engine that serves stale rationale is worse than none, because it supplies confident justification for an obsolete decision; without a decay/invalidation mechanism the layer silently accumulates wrong context.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Jeffrey Ng
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Context engineering for AI agents and why infrastructure and primitives are no longer the primary bottleneck in agent development.
  • Purpose: To demonstrate that context engineering is the next major frontier in AI agent development and to explain why humans currently act as context layers for agents. Building AI agents has become trivial due to mature cloud infrastructure and primitives like Flue, Vercel Eve, and Mastra. However, agents still fail reliably because they lack context. This talk explores the shift from infrastructure challenges to context engineering, introducing the concept of a Context Engine that provides relevant, reconciled, governed, and well-timed context across tools, docs, code, and conversations, contrasting it with the raw access provided by MCP (Model Context Protocol).

Topic Map

The Evolution of Agent Building

  • Explanation: Six months ago, building an agent required an extensive team effort and a quarter of work across session management, checkpointing, orchestration, retry logic, sandbox infrastructure, execution isolation, observability, multi-channel adapters, and replay/debugging. Today, modern primitives and cloud frameworks have abstracted this complexity away.
  • Key claims:
    • Building agents is trivial now.
    • Infrastructure components like sandbox isolation and state persistence are now solved by modern frameworks.
    • Agent runtimes like Flue on Cloudflare handle almost all infrastructure requirements out of the box.
  • Examples:
    • Flue, Vercel Eve, and Mastra as modern agent frameworks.
  • Terminology:
    • Session management
    • State persistence
    • Sandbox infrastructure
    • Observability
  • Why it matters: Developers can now focus on core agent logic and customer value rather than infrastructure.

Why Agents Fail: The Missing Context

  • Explanation: Even with easy agent setup, agents still get things confidently wrong because they lack organizational and situational context, such as past decisions, tribal knowledge, migration plans, and post-mortems.
  • Key claims:
    • Agents lack a full picture because they miss tribal knowledge and post-mortem discussions.
    • Without proper context, background agents make silent mistakes that misinform teams.
    • Humans currently act as the context layer by babysitting agents.
  • Examples:
    • An AI agent fixing a linear ticket recommended reenabling async dispatch because it lacked context that a support engineer had explicitly disabled it due to a past outage.
  • Terminology:
    • Silent failure
    • Tribal knowledge
    • Post-mortem
    • Context layer
  • Why it matters: Without context, agent-generated solutions can cause real production outages and propagate misinformation.

The Context Engine vs. MCP

  • Explanation: While MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects agents to various data sources and returns raw matches, a Context Engine synthesizes sources, ranks by task relevance, resolves contradictions, and enforces permissions.
  • Key claims:
    • MCP provides access, but access is not understanding.
    • MCP floods the agent with raw matches, increasing context window costs and forcing the agent to decide what to believe.
    • A Context Engine delivers a synthesized understanding that an agent can act on directly.
  • Examples:
    • Connecting Slack MCP, Linear MCP, and GitHub MCP versus using Unblocked's Context Engine.
  • Terminology:
    • Model Context Protocol (MCP)
    • Context engine
    • Targeted retrieval
    • Conflict resolution
  • Why it matters: Context engines solve the signal-to-noise problem and prevent token bloat while respecting organizational permissions.

Key Points

Agents lack contextual awareness

  • Explanation: Agents have instructions, tools, skills, and code, but they lack the underlying 'why' behind architectural decisions and tribal knowledge.
  • Evidence: An agent suggesting a fix for linear tickets without knowing why a previous engineer disabled async dispatch.
  • Practical implication: Engineers must provide synthesized contextual intelligence to agents rather than raw data dumps.

The definition of an agent is now minimal code

  • Explanation: With frameworks like Flue on Cloudflare, defining an agent requires only selecting a model, setting instructions, defining tools and skills, and choosing sandbox locations.
  • Evidence: Code snippet showing defineAgent using Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet with simple configuration parameters.
  • Practical implication: Agent creation code is extremely compact, shifting developer focus entirely to workflow and data relevance.

Context Engine pillars

  • Explanation: A context engine operates on relevance, reconciliation, governance, and delivery.
  • Evidence: Comparison slide showing how Unblocked processes sources (code, docs, tickets, conversations) into structured context.
  • Practical implication: Ensures agents receive precise, permissioned, and timely information without polluting context windows.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Context Engine Framework

  • How it works: Merges signals from all company data sources, resolves conflicts, enforces permissions, and delivers synthesized context tailored to the user or agent task.
  • Components:
    • Unified system context
    • Conflict resolution
    • Token optimization
    • Targeted retrieval
    • Personalized relevance
    • Permission enforcement
  • When to use: When deploying AI agents for code generation, code review, ticket triage, and incident management in enterprise environments.

Examples & Case Studies

An agent was deployed to enrich Linear tickets and recommended reenabling async dispatch.

  • Illustrates: The danger of an agent lacking post-mortem context and tribal knowledge.
  • Lesson: Agents operating without organizational context will repeat past mistakes and cause outages.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Building agent infrastructure is no longer a major engineering hurdle thanks to modern frameworks.
    • Connecting multiple MCP servers without a context layer floods agents with irrelevant raw data.
  • Strategic:
    • Context engineering is the critical bottleneck and differentiator for production AI agents.
    • Organizations need a dedicated context engine to model institutional knowledge across code, docs, tickets, and chats.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How do context engines handle real-time updates to tribal knowledge?
    • What are the latency tradeoffs of running a context engine query before every agent action?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Building agents required a team effort and a quarter of work six months ago (timeline claim)
  • Flue on Cloudflare handles all 9 agent runtime requirements (technological claim)

Notable Quotes

"Building agents is trivial now. Context is the next frontier." (at 0:14) "MCP is great at access, but access isn't understanding." (at 16:39) "The gap is not intelligence. It's context." (at 20:36)

Compressed Summary

  • Agent infrastructure and building blocks are now commoditized and trivial to set up.
  • Agents fail in production because they lack tribal knowledge, intent, and historical context.
  • MCP provides raw data access, whereas a Context Engine provides synthesized understanding and conflict resolution.
  • Context engines ensure relevance, reconciliation, governance, and timely delivery of enterprise knowledge.
  • Keywords: context engineering, ai agents, mcp, unblocked, llm architecture
  • Core insight: The primary barrier to effective AI agents is no longer model intelligence or infrastructure primitives, but the lack of a centralized context engine to deliver relevant organizational knowledge.

  - Personalized relevance
  - Permission enforcement
- **When to use**: When deploying AI agents for code generation, code review, ticket triage, and incident management in enterprise environments.
## Examples & Case Studies
### An agent was deployed to enrich Linear tickets and recommended reenabling async dispatch.
- **Illustrates**: The danger of an agent lacking post-mortem context and tribal knowledge.
- **Lesson**: Agents operating without organizational context will repeat past mistakes and cause outages.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Building agent infrastructure is no longer a major engineering hurdle thanks to modern frameworks.
  - Connecting multiple MCP servers without a context layer floods agents with irrelevant raw data.
- **Strategic**:
  - Context engineering is the critical bottleneck and differentiator for production AI agents.
  - Organizations need a dedicated context engine to model institutional knowledge across code, docs, tickets, and chats.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How do context engines handle real-time updates to tribal knowledge?
  - What are the latency tradeoffs of running a context engine query before every agent action?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Building agents required a team effort and a quarter of work six months ago (timeline claim)
- Flue on Cloudflare handles all 9 agent runtime requirements (technological claim)
## Notable Quotes
> "Building agents is trivial now. Context is the next frontier." (at 0:14)
> "MCP is great at access, but access isn't understanding." (at 16:39)
> "The gap is not intelligence. It's context." (at 20:36)
## Compressed Summary
- Agent infrastructure and building blocks are now commoditized and trivial to set up.
- Agents fail in production because they lack tribal knowledge, intent, and historical context.
- MCP provides raw data access, whereas a Context Engine provides synthesized understanding and conflict resolution.
- Context engines ensure relevance, reconciliation, governance, and timely delivery of enterprise knowledge.
- **Keywords**: context engineering, ai agents, mcp, unblocked, llm architecture
- **Core insight**: The primary barrier to effective AI agents is no longer model intelligence or infrastructure primitives, but the lack of a centralized context engine to deliver relevant organizational knowledge.
